introduction: This fourth Sunday of Easter is Good Shepherd Sunday, a day of prayer for vocations. Jesus says, My sheep hear my voice; I know them, and they follow me; no one can take them out of my hand. Paul and Barnabas bring the Gospel to the nations. John sees a great multitude from every nation, whom the Lamb shepherds to springs of living water. Let us listen to our shepherd's voice.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, we are the Lord's people, the sheep of his flock. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For our Pope, our bishop and our priests: that they may be good shepherds after the heart of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood, the diaconate and religious life: that young people may hear and follow the voice of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries who bring the Gospel to new peoples: that they may be filled with joy and the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have come out of great suffering: that the Lamb may lead them to springs of living water and wipe away every tear. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may know the voice of our shepherd and follow him. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, no one can snatch your sheep from your hand. Keep us close to you, raise up shepherds for your Church, and lead us to eternal life. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: My sheep hear my voice
reflection.body:
Today's Gospel is very short, but it holds a great promise. Jesus says, "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand."

There are three verbs for the sheep: they hear, they are known, they follow. Christian life begins with listening to the voice of Jesus, in his word, in prayer, in the Church. It rests on being known personally by him. And it means following him, wherever he leads.

Then comes the promise: no one can snatch us from his hand. And Jesus adds that his Father holds us too: "No one is able to snatch them out of my Father's hand. I and the Father are one." We are held by God himself.

The first reading shows the Good Shepherd's voice going out to all peoples. When some reject their message, Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles, quoting the prophet: "I have set you as a light for the Gentiles." Even when they are driven out, "The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit."

In the Book of Revelation, John sees the result: "a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages." They have come through great suffering, and now "the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them and leads them to springs of life-giving waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes." The Shepherd is also the Lamb who gave his life.

Today the Church prays for vocations. Pray for the priests you know, and for young people who may be called. And this week, take time to listen to the shepherd's voice in the Gospel, and follow where he leads.
